prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1155; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a side impact collision at an intersection involving two vehicles. The claimant is represented by counsel, and the claim file has been opened for review.

Entry 2: Obtained the police report and statements from the other driver and two independent witnesses. All of them describe the collision the same way, with the other vehicle entering the intersection and striking the driver's side.

Entry 3: Reviewed the photographs taken at the scene. The damage pattern is largely consistent with the impact described, concentrated on the driver's side doors and rear quarter panel.

Entry 4: Confirmed through the police report and witness accounts that the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the crash. The driver is named on the policy and coverage was active on the loss date.

Entry 5: Reviewed the policy inception records and the vehicle's prior claim history. Nothing suggests the damage predates the coverage period, and no earlier damage to the vehicle is on record.

Entry 6: Received the medical records from the claimant's counsel. The reported wrist fracture fits the kind of force expected from a side impact of this type, and no prior injury to the same area appears in the records.

Entry 7: Reviewed the treatment timeline. Care followed a typical course, with treatment gradually reducing as the claimant's condition improved and follow-up visits became less frequent.

Entry 8: Spoke with counsel regarding the claimant's account. The claimant has given the same description of the collision in each conversation, and the account aligns with the statements already on file.

Entry 9: Reviewed the repair estimate against the photographs and the reported impact. The scope of repairs is mostly in line with the described collision, and the estimate has been forwarded for internal review.

Entry 10: Updated the file with the current status of the injury and property components. Liability evaluation is progressing, and the claim will be reassessed once the remaining medical bills are received.
